what: The first host evidence for the only Office.js-reaching behaviour change in v0.6.1.
build: 0fde152, whose shipped bytes are identical to v0.6.1 — `git diff v0.6.1..HEAD -- src manifest*.xml vite.config.ts` is empty
host: PowerPoint on the web, pane stamp 0fde152, deck Presentation64
why: `src/core/elements.ts` gained `desc` on all five builders between 454303d (the last round-validated build before the release) and v0.6.1, and `scene.desc` flows `-> opts.altText -> Shape.altTextDescription` at three call sites in powerpoint.ts. That is a PowerPointApi 1.10 write. No scenario in selftest.ts touches Elements — grep it for harvey/kpiCard/elements and the count is 0 — so rounds 455-459 were green five times without ever asking. The manifest ships five ribbon deep links straight at these buttons, which is what a certification tester clicks first.
method: Clicked each element's own button by DOM id inside the pane's frame (all five share the accessible name "Insert", so a name lookup cannot tell them apart), then read the selected slide back through Office.js with `items/altTextDescription` NAMED in the load.

confirmed.flow: Process flow: Scope, Design, Build, Launch. Design highlighted.

unverified.table: NOT a defect, and not confirmed either. The button was enabled, the click was accepted, and the insert was attempted at 23 shapes. The host then went silent and the pane reported it: 'Failed: PowerPoint did not respond while drawing shapes 1-10 of 23 (45s) | at=drawing the chart's shapes'. The slide's shape count was 52 before and after. Same 45s silent-host stall that blind-skipped `insert onto a slide that already has content` in round 458.

conclusion: ALL FIVE Elements write a correct, element-specific altTextDescription on a real host, confirmed in a single run on 2026-09-18. The 1.10 write reaches PowerPoint and the accessibility description a user gets is the one the engine built. READ THE SITTINGS IN ORDER — the corrections are the useful part. This file said the fifth element was untested, then that it was a grouping refusal, then that it was the element, then that it was session age. It was the instrument.

secondSitting.why: To finish the table element, and to re-run the probe after it was fixed to tell `could not ask` from `asked and the answer was wrong`.
secondSitting.reconfirmed: A hand read of the settled slide returned the same four descriptions, each on a shape named PowerChart: 'Harvey ball, 75% filled.', 'Checkbox, yes.', 'Process flow: Scope, Design, Build, Launch. Design highlighted.', 'Revenue: €4.2m +12% vs LY (up).'. The host reported PowerPointApi 1.8/1.9/1.10 = true, 1.11 = false, so the 1.10 gate was open throughout.
secondSitting.table: STILL NOT CONFIRMED, and the reason is the SAME 45s stall as the first sitting — not a second, different one. RETRACTED 2026-09-17, same day, by a review that counted the parts: this entry said 'its parts arrived — rule-top, rule-header, cell-text-0-0..0-4, cell-text-1-0..1-2 — and NEVER GROUPED', and called grouping the new blocker. That is ten shapes, `SHAPES_PER_SYNC` is 10 (`powerpoint.ts:9755`), and they are the first ten of the scene in order. `buildTableScene` (`elements.ts:525`) pushes a `cell-text-<r>-<c>` for every column of every row unconditionally and a `rule-bottom` unconditionally under the default `rules` style, so a COMPLETED table can never end at 3 cells in row 1 with no bottom rule. What is on the slide is one sync's worth of a 23-shape draw — character for character the batch the first sitting watched the pane die in, 'PowerPoint did not respond while drawing shapes 1-10 of 23 (45s)'. Grouping was never REACHED, which is not the same as refused, and the difference is the whole point of this file. What is true: no shape named PowerChart carrying a 'Table, N rows by M columns.' description exists on the slide. Why is unsettled, and the instrument that would settle it is the pane's own status line, which was not read.
secondSitting.hostCondition: Badly degraded, and this is what the sitting mostly measured. Across four probe runs the host stalled reads for 45-60s and left around sixty loose parts — harvey-fill-f0..f22, step-0..3, kpi-box, check-box — from inserts that produced no group. WHETHER THOSE WERE REFUSALS OR TRUNCATED DRAWS IS NOT ESTABLISHED: an earlier version of this entry said 'refused to group 3 of 5 elements at a time', which reads a cause off the same evidence that a draw stopping mid-batch would leave. The probe cannot separate them and neither can a shape list; only the pane's status line can. What IS established and is the point of the sitting: every element that DID group carried its correct description, and not one grouped shape was missing one.
secondSitting.aHostQuirkWorthKnowing: `presentation.setSelectedSlides([newSlideId])` returns without error and `slides.items.length` goes up, but `getSelectedSlides().getItemAt(0)` keeps returning the previously selected slide. Three attempts to give the probe a clean slide all silently read the old one. It changes none of the verdicts — the probe diffs shape ids per run, so what was already there is excluded either way — but a future reader should not believe an added slide is a selected one.
secondSitting.whatTheProbeLearned: It reported `0 of 5 elements carried an altTextDescription`, exit 1, against a build whose descriptions were sitting on that slide as it printed. Three separate confusions, all the same shape: a silent host counted as a wrong answer, a shape read mid-insert counted as a finished one, and an insert that never grouped counted as a description that was never written. Each now has a named cause in the verdict and its own line in the report.

thirdSitting.why: To finish the table element on a healthy host, after a browser restart cleared thirteen orphaned Chrome processes and a full cycle (rounds 460-462) came back 18/19, 19/19, 19/19.
thirdSitting.method: Same probe, on a slide cleared to ZERO shapes first, and — the change that mattered — reading `#host-note`, the pane's own status line, on every element that did not simply pass. The second sitting's correction said that instrument 'was not read'; `readNoteScript` now reads it.
thirdSitting.result: FOUR OF FIVE CARRY THEIR DESCRIPTION, measured in a single run on a clean slide: harvey 'Harvey ball, 75% filled.' (11s), check 'Checkbox, yes.' (11s), flow 'Process flow: Scope, Design, Build, Launch. Design highlighted.' (23s), kpi 'Revenue: €4.2m +12% vs LY (up).' (12s).
thirdSitting.tableIsNowMEASUREDRatherThanInferred: The pane said it, twice in a row, word for word: 'Failed: PowerPoint did not respond while drawing shapes 1-10 of 23 (45s) | at=drawing the chart's shapes'. Ten loose shapes on the slide ARE shapes 1-10 of 23. So the blocker is the host stalling on the FIRST draw batch — not a grouping refusal (the second sitting's retracted claim) and not the 1.10 write, which is never reached. Four occurrences now: the first sitting, and three today.
thirdSitting.aHYPOTHESIS_NOT_A_FINDING: It is not shape COUNT. `harvey` is 24 shapes and completes in 11s; `table` is 23 and dies on its first batch of 10. What differs is composition: harvey's first ten are `harvey-ring` plus nine `harvey-fill-*`, all geometric, zero text. The table's first ten are `rule-top`, `rule-header` and EIGHT `cell-text-*`, i.e. eight `addTextBox` calls in one sync. The other elements carry text in ones and twos and are fine. That points at a batch dense in text boxes rather than at size — but it is one comparison on one host and nothing has varied the composition deliberately, so it is a hypothesis to test, not a result. The experiment is cheap: draw ten text boxes in one sync and time it against ten rectangles.
thirdSitting.whatTheUserGETS: On this host, clicking `table` leaves ten loose shapes on the slide and a failure message. The pane reports it honestly rather than failing silently, which is the behaviour working. Whether the wreckage should be swept is a separate question and is not answered here.

fourthSitting.headline: ALL FIVE ELEMENTS ARE NOW CONFIRMED ON A REAL HOST. The fifth, `table`, was never broken — it drew first-in-session on an empty slide as one grouped shape carrying 'Table, 4 rows by 5 columns.', read straight off the slide.
fourthSitting.whatWasWrongWithTheThirdSitting: It concluded the table 'does not draw', from five failures that were all its LAST element. `ELEMENTS` runs in a fixed order and `table` is last, so every run measured it latest in the session. Position was a confound and the probe never said so; it reported the element as broken five times.
fourthSitting.theControls: table 1st on an empty slide -> Done. table/check/flow/kpi as 1st-4th -> all Done. harvey 5th onto four element groups -> Done. table 6th onto five groups -> Failed at shapes 11-20 of 23. table 5th with the slide CLEARED first -> Failed the same way, so it is not slide load. table 1st again straight afterwards -> Done, so it is not a poisoned session either.
fourthSitting.soTheVariableIsSESSIONAGE: Not the element, not the slide, not the shape count. The archive already holds this under office-js#3565 (syncs getting progressively longer, a restart resetting it) and #6329 (the web host forcing a full presentation save on every sync). What the table adds is that it is the first thing to cross the 45s budget when that cost rises.
fourthSitting.whyTheTableFirst: `SHAPES_PER_SYNC` caps SHAPES and the cost is STATEMENTS. Measured on `scripts/textbox-cost-probe.mjs`: the table's first batch styled the way `addText` styles it costs 1641ms against 498ms for the same ten shapes unstyled — 3.4x for identical geometry. A text node is 20 statements and a rect 7, so the table's batch is ~174 statements against harvey's ~70, and both are 'ten shapes'.
fourthSitting.hypothesesTheBenchKilled: COMPOSITION: ten text boxes 571ms against ten rectangles 419ms, 1.3x — refuted. THE EMPTY CORNER CELL: `buildTableScene` emits a text node for every cell including the blank one at 0,0, and the failed insert's shapes read back with `cell-text-0-0` carrying '' — the sharpest candidate available, and adding exactly it to the styled batch gave 1628ms against 1641ms. Refuted.
fourthSitting.fixed: `elements-probe.mjs` now clears the slide between elements and documents why.

doesNotCover: A second host. Everything here is PowerPoint on the web, on one machine, and the session-age effect is exactly the kind of thing that could differ.
Whether budgeting by STATEMENTS instead of shapes would fix it. That is the remedy direction and it is not implemented — one host, one sitting, and two hypotheses already dead here.
PowerPoint on Windows or Mac desktop. This is the web host only.
Whether the description is what a screen reader should ideally say. This checks that the engine's `desc` ARRIVED, not that the copy is good.
n = 1 per element, one slide, one session.
theProbeCostThreeSelfInflictedWounds: It anchored on `tab "Chart"` copied from round.mjs's readiness check. This pane's tabs are Elements/Agenda/Automation, so it reported `no pane on screen` against a pane that was open and healthy.

It passed `--regex` to the CLI's `find`, which takes plain text — the driver applies its regex in JS afterwards, in `refFor`. And it took the FIRST ref in the output rather than the one on the matching line, which `refFor`'s own comment warns lands you in the OneDrive document where `PowerPoint` is undefined.

Worst: its parser could not read the CLI's escaped quotes, so `JSON.parse` threw and every element reported `the host would not list the slide` while the host was answering perfectly. A parser that cannot read the answer reports the same thing as a feature that was never written.

fifthSitting.headline: FIVE OF FIVE, exit 0, in one run: harvey 19s, check 14s, flow 12s, kpi 13s, table 31s — the table carrying "Table, 4 rows by 5 columns."
fifthSitting.theCause: THE PROBE CAUSED THE FAILURE IT REPORTED. `settleReads` polled the SLIDE every 4s through the draw — a PowerPoint.run per poll, interleaved with the renderer's own batches, on a host that forces a full presentation save on every sync (office-js#6329).
fifthSitting.theControl: Same fresh session, same cleared slide, same element, polling the ONLY difference. Without polling: "Done." With polling every 4s: "Failed: PowerPoint did not respond while drawing shapes 11-20 of 23 (45s)", and the poll results read X,20,20,20,... — the first read timing out against the draw, then the shape count frozen at 20.
fifthSitting.whyOnlyTheTable: The other four have short draws and survive the contention; the table has the longest and is hit repeatedly. Every "table FAILS" this probe ever reported was this.
fifthSitting.theFix: `settleReads` now waits on `#host-note`'s busy CLASS — a DOM read costing the host nothing — and makes exactly ONE host call, after the pane says it has settled. The stable-id counting and the 24s quiescence floor are gone; they were guessing at what the pane already knew.
fifthSitting.hypothesesKilledGettingHere: composition (1.3x), the empty corner cell (1628ms against 1641ms), session age (the table drew fine as the SIXTH insert in a fresh session), and slide load (clearing the slide did not save it).
fifthSitting.theOneRealFinding: The batch limit counts SHAPES and the cost is STATEMENTS — 1641ms against 498ms for identical geometry, 3.4x. Recorded in BACKLOG section 3. It is not the cause of anything here.
